Instead of typing out the patterns (which you can still do if you so wish), you can drag and connect the blocks to build regex step by step (with some helpful error warnings if using non-compatible blocks). entry.title: MongoDB arrays: sort order and comparison
entry.summary: Arrays in MongoDB are ordered lists of values, and querying them can be confusing because a field might be a scalar value in one document and an array in another. Unlike SQL databases, there's no need to choose between one-to-one, one-to-many, or many-to-many relationships once for all future data. Within the limits of schema validation, each document can have a unique schema, allowing fields to be any data type, scalar or array. When indexing or querying a collection, field names are used, and operations like filtering or sorting must work for all documents, regardless of its data type. This flexibility can lead to behavior that may seem strange to developers accustomed to the strict schemas of SQL databases. entry.title: Object Storage vs Block Storage: Key Differences Explained
entry.summary: It’s important to know the main differences between Object Storage vs Block Storage when you need to find the right storage solution for your business or application. This complete guide explains everything you need to know about these two types of storage architectures, so you can make a smart choice that meets your needs. Block storage breaks up data into blocks of a set size, each with its own unique ID. It’s like a regular hard drive, with data stored in certain places that the operating system can get to directly. Each block works on its own, which makes reading and writing very fast. Block storage looks like a raw block device to the operating system, just like a real hard drive. After that, the OS can format this storage with any file system it knows how to use. Block storage is very fast and efficient for apps that need to change data often because it gives you direct, low-level access. Data stored in fixed-size blocks (typically 512 bytes to 64KB) Direct access through operating system High IOPS (Input/Output Operations Per Second) Low latency for read/write operations Suitable for structured data Object storage keeps data in separate objects in a flat address space called buckets or containers. Block storage has a hierarchical structure, but object storage has a simple namespace where each object has the data, metadata, and a globally unique identifier. Files turn into objects that are stored in buckets with lots of metadata in object storage systems. REST APIs and HTTP protocols let applications get to these objects. This web-friendly method makes object storage perfect for cloud-native apps and systems that are spread out. Key characteristics of object storage: Data stored as complete objects Flat namespace structure REST API access via HTTP/HTTPS Rich metadata capabilities Highly scalable architecture Built-in redundancy and durability Read full article: https://serveravatar.com/object-storage-vs-block-storage/

Set Your Income: Enter your monthly or hourly net income and the number of working days.
Browse Online Shops: Prices automatically appear in work hours alongside the original amount.
That’s it. Every time you shop, you get an instant reality check: the hours you’ve worked to earn that product are now front and center. Instant Conversion: See work hours alongside prices, automatically. Fully Personalized: Enter your monthly or hourly net income and the number of working days along the number of daily working hours. Spend Smarter: Avoid purchases that aren’t worth your time. Future Expansion: More stores will be supported soon. Check out the project on GitHub or install it directly from the Chrome Web Store and see how it works for yourself. This project is open-source, so you can: Share it with friends and colleagues Report issues or submit pull requests on GitHub If you love it, leaving a Chrome Web Store review helps others discover it too. Shopping suddenly becomes less about impulse and more about intention. Start seeing your money, and your time, in a whole new way. ⏳💸

entry.title: Tomcat set Windows cmd title
entry.summary:
When you open multiple tomcat windows, it is difficult to distinguish which window is which project. Setting the window name can help distinguish. Enter the bin directory of tomcat, such as T:\apache-tomcat-9.0.60-windows-x64\apache-tomcat-9.0.60\bin, find the catalina.bat file, and open it with a text editor. You can see in the bottom of the description, there is a parameter called TITLE, and the default is Tomcat. You can modify it according to your needs. It can have spaces. rem TITLE (Optional) Specify the title of Tomcat window. The default rem TITLE is Tomcat if it's not specified. rem Example (all one line) rem set TITLE=Tomcat.Cluster#1.Server#1 [%DATE% %TIME%]
Search for TITLE in the file, and find the following section. Fill in your name after set TITLE. :doStart shift rem Set the title of the window rem if "%TITLE%" == "" set TITLE=Tomcat if "%TITLE%" == "" set TITLE=YOURNAME YOURSUBNAME set _EXECJAVA=start "%TITLE%" %_RUNJAVA% if not ""%1"" == ""-security"" goto execCmd shift echo Using Security Manager set "SECURITY_POLICY_FILE=%CATALINA_BASE%\conf\catalina.policy" goto execCmd
